name: Yogi Tea
description: The spiced tea poured at every Solstice: black tea simmered slowly with whole spices and finished with the milk of your choice. Warming and grounding — the first cup after Sadhana.
benefits: Warms the body and settles digestion after early-morning practice|Cinnamon, ginger and black pepper are traditionally used to support circulation|Cardamom and cloves soothe the stomach and freshen the breath
ingredients: Water|Cinnamon sticks|Green cardamom pods|Whole cloves|Black peppercorns|Fresh ginger|Black tea|Oat or dairy milk

name: Kitcheree with mung beans
description: Mung beans and basmati rice cooked into a soft, savory porridge with ghee or oil, ginger, turmeric and greens. The classic cleansing meal of the yogic kitchen — complete protein that is easy on the stomach.
benefits: Easy to digest: a mono-diet staple during cleansing days|Mung beans and rice together form a complete protein|Turmeric and ginger are traditionally used to calm inflammation and support digestion
ingredients: Whole mung beans|Basmati rice|Onion|Fresh ginger|Garlic|Turmeric|Cumin|Coriander|Seasonal greens|Ghee or coconut oil|Sea salt

name: Golden milk
description: Turmeric paste warmed in oat or almond milk with a little almond oil and honey — the evening drink of the Kundalini Yoga tradition, taken to look after the joints and the spine.
benefits: Turmeric is traditionally used for supple joints and a calm inflammatory response|Warm milk with almond oil before bed eases the body toward sleep|A gentle, lightly sweet way to end the day
ingredients: Turmeric root or paste|Oat or almond milk|Cold-pressed almond oil|Honey or maple syrup|Black pepper

name: Lentil soup
description: Red lentils simmered with carrots, celery and cumin until they fall apart, finished with lemon and parsley. The arrival-night soup: simple, filling and ready whenever your bus comes in.
benefits: High in plant protein and fiber — sustaining after a day of travel|Iron and folate from the lentils|Light enough for a late evening

name: Dal with ginger
description: Yellow split peas cooked down with a generous amount of fresh ginger, turmeric and a tempering of cumin seeds in ghee.
benefits: Ginger warms the digestion on cool December days|Plant protein that pairs with rice into a complete meal|Naturally gluten-free
ingredients: Yellow split peas|Fresh ginger|Turmeric|Cumin seeds|Tomato|Ghee or oil|Cilantro|Sea salt

name: Dal
description: Langar dal: black lentils and chickpeas slow-cooked overnight the way they are served in the Gurdwara kitchen — creamy, mildly spiced and shared by everyone regardless of who they are.
benefits: A complete, sustaining meal when eaten with roti|Slow cooking makes the lentils gentle on the stomach|Prepared as seva and offered to all

name: Oatmeal with dates and almonds
description: Rolled oats cooked in oat milk with chopped dates, toasted almonds and a pinch of cinnamon.
benefits: Slow-release energy through a long morning|Beta-glucan fiber from the oats|Dates sweeten the bowl without added sugar

name: Warm rice porridge
description: Short-grain rice simmered until creamy with a little cardamom — a quiet, easy breakfast for a White Tantric Yoga® morning.
benefits: Very easy to digest before a long day of sitting|Gentle and warming|Naturally gluten-free

name: Millet porridge
description: Whole millet cooked soft in almond milk and finished with a swirl of tahini.
benefits: Millet is alkalizing and naturally gluten-free|Magnesium and B vitamins|Keeps you full through the morning kriyas

name: Miso vegetable soup

name: Squash curry

name: Coconut rice
description: Jasmine rice steamed in coconut milk with a little lime zest.

name: Kheer
description: Rice pudding slow-cooked in milk with cardamom, raisins and almonds — the sweet that closes the Langar.

name: Roti

name: Warm almond milk with cardamom
description: Almond milk warmed with cardamom and a touch of maple — a soft first light on the morning after the Solstice.

name: Steamed winter greens
description: Kale, collards and chard steamed briefly and dressed with lemon and olive oil.

name: Vegetable broth
description: A clear broth of root vegetables, celery and herbs, kept light on purpose for the first White Tantric Yoga® day.
benefits: Hydrating and easy to digest during long sitting|Minerals without heaviness
